sentences.text: Nullotitan is a lithostrotian titanosaur belonging to the class Saurischia, a group of large, long-necked dinosaurs.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a cervical vertebra found in 1981, tail vertebrae, ribs, a scapula, and leg bones.
This individual was more than 20 meters long and weighed 20 tons.
The neck vertebra measures 45 centimeters in length and 22 centimeters in height, excluding the broken arch, and contains many small internal air chambers called camellae.
The first tail vertebra measures approximately 25 centimeters in length and 40 centimeters in width.
A referred humerus — a bone from the same species found separately — is 114 centimeters long and has a robustness index of 0.28.
The front and middle tail vertebrae feature large depressions on their sides and undersides that do not penetrate the bone wall.
The fibula exhibits a distinct S-shaped curve when viewed from the front or back.
Excavations revealed a new fauna across 2,000 square kilometers containing six bone concentrations linked to the original discovery.
Titanosaur eggshells and sauropod teeth have been found in the same geological formation.
Remains of Nullotitan were found in the Chorrillo Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, where geologist Francisco E. Nullo first noticed sauropod bones at the Estancia Alta Vista site in 1980.
José Bonaparte excavated a large cervical vertebra in 1981 and reported it as cf. Antarctosaurus.

The genus Nullotitan honors paleontologist Francisco Nullo and links it to a "Greek titan," referring to the great race of powerful giants from Greek mythology, while the species name glaciaris refers to the Perito Moreno Glacier visible near the fossil discovery site.
Researchers suggest that epaxial tendons may have been anchored to the tail, holding it upward.
The large retractor muscle Musculus caudofemoralis, which pushed the femur backward, extended to the sixteenth vertebra.

Novas and colleagues initially classified Nullotitan as a colossosaurian titanosaur in 2019 without a phylogenetic test, placing it within Titanosauria in Colossosauria, though its precise relationships remain unclear.
Later analyses recovered Nullotitan as a lithostrotian titanosaur outside the group Colossosauria.
The holotype fossils date to the Campanian–Maastrichtian stages of the lower Chorrillo Formation, and Nullotitan lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Nullotitan lived alongside the ornithopod dinosaur Isasicursor, and the same formation contains fossils of the theropod Maip and the birds Kookne and Yatenavis.
It is currently unknown whether the newly discovered series of five middle tail vertebrae at a different location have been excavated.
